objective: Understand how wind lifts a kite and where to launch.

narration.text: A kite rises when wind pushes against its sail and the line holds it at an angle.
Steady wind gives even lift, while gusts make the kite dive and climb suddenly.
Launch with the wind at your back in an open space with no trees nearby.

teachBack.question: Why is steady wind better than gusty wind for flying?
Where should you stand when you launch?
rubric: wind at your back|back to the wind

followUp.question: What do you give up by flying only on calm days?

transfer.scenario: You are flying at a beach where the wind comes off the sea.
rubric: wind direction|which way the wind blows
